Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroGreen Energy Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AeroGreen Energy's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Lisa Wong, Chief Technology Officer; Tom Greer, Chief Sustainability Officer; Karen Lopez, Chief Operating Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Strategy Officer; and Emily Novak, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Harlan.

John Harlan:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. AeroGreen Energy continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in the third quarter. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

It's a pleasure to be with you all today as we wrap up another strong quarter for AeroGreen Energy. Q3 revenues came in at $285 million, up 28% year-over-year, driven by 750 MW of new solar and wind capacity coming online across our U.S. and European portfolios. Adjusted EBITDA hit $92 million, with margins expanding to 32.3%—our strongest in two years—thanks to optimized operations and maintenance costs and favorable power purchase agreement pricing amid tightening grid supply-demand dynamics.

Looking ahead, our strategic priorities for Q4 2024 and fiscal 2025 center on three pillars: accelerating our development pipeline to 8 GW by year-end, scaling next-generation clean tech integrations like long-duration energy storage and green hydrogen, and capitalizing on regional tailwinds through disciplined mergers and acquisitions and partnerships. We're laser-focused on utility-scale solar PV, onshore wind, and emerging offshore wind opportunities. Our backlog stands at 4.2 GW under construction or late-stage development, with another 3.8 GW in advanced greenfield pipelines—bringing total visibility to over 8 GW. For Q4, we expect to energize 1.1 GW, including the 450 MW Desert Bloom bifacial solar farm in Arizona, leveraging our proprietary tracker tech with 25% higher yield versus fixed-tilt systems. This positions us to capture $450-500 million in revenue recognition this quarter alone, up 35% from Q3.

For FY2025, we're guiding to 2.5-2.8 GW of new additions, driving consolidated revenues to $1.45-1.55 billion—a 25-30% increase over 2024. EBITDA guidance is $420-460 million, with margins stabilizing at 28-30%, factoring in some engineering, procurement, and construction cost inflation from polysilicon supply constraints. Key enablers include our 85% contracted portfolio—primarily long-term PPAs with investment-grade off-takers like Google and Microsoft—insulating us from merchant volatility. Internal rate of return targets remain north of 12% on a levered basis, bolstered by Investment Tax Credit and Production Tax Credit extensions under the Inflation Reduction Act.

North America is our growth engine, representing 65% of our pipeline. The IRA's production tax credits have supercharged our U.S. Southwest solar builds, with levelized cost of energy for our utility-scale projects now sub-$25/MWh—competitive with supercritical coal retirements. We're also advancing 800 MW of onshore wind in Texas' ERCOT market, where capacity factors are hitting 45% thanks to taller hubs and larger rotors akin to Vestas' platforms.

In Europe, which accounts for 25% of our FY2025 revenue mix, we're prioritizing offshore wind under REPowerEU. Our 300 MW stake in the Dutch Borssele extension hits financial close in Q1 2025, with first power by H2 2026. Permitting headwinds persist, but we've de-risked via our €200 million JV with Siemens Gamesa for fixed-bottom turbines.

Asia-Pacific rounds out at 10%, with early traction in India's 500 GW renewable target. We're reaching final investment decision on a 200 MW floating solar hybrid on the Ganges by mid-2025, partnering with Adani Green for EPC, tapping into their supply chain efficiencies.

We're not just building gigawatts; we're future-proofing the grid. In energy storage, our 1.2 GWh pipeline—up 50% YoY—includes iron-air long-duration systems, targeting 100-hour discharge for renewables curtailment. Q4 sees our first 150 MW/600 MWh battery energy storage system deployment co-located with the Desert Bloom solar, unlocking ancillary services revenue at $15-20/kW-month in CAISO.

Green hydrogen is our high-growth beta: We've allocated $150 million capex for a 50 MW electrolyzer at our Texas wind site, using PEM tech to produce 4,000 tonnes/year at under $2/kg—aligned with DOE H2Hub targets. This feeds into offtake discussions with Air Products, with first revenues in H2 2025 contributing 5% to EBITDA growth.

R&D spend rises to 4% of revenues in 2025 ($60 million), focused on perovskite-silicon tandem cells with partners, pushing module efficiencies to 30%+ and halving balance-of-system costs.

With $450 million in liquidity and a net debt-to-EBITDA of 2.1x, we're pursuing bolt-ons. Expect $300-400 million in tuck-in acquisitions, like our recent $120 million buy of a 250 MW California development portfolio. Shareholder returns include a 20% dividend hike to $0.45/share and $100 million share repurchase authorization.

Q4 revenues: $320-340 million. FY2025 top-line growth: 25-30%, with 15% CAGR through 2027 on a 12 GW pipeline. Trends favor us: Global renewable additions hit 510 GW in 2024, with storage deployments doubling YoY. Supply chains are stabilizing—module prices down 15% QoQ—though interest rates and tariffs pose risks to our hedging.

Forward-looking risks include supply chain bottlenecks, interconnection queues—we've derisked 90% of our U.S. pipeline—and policy shifts. We're well-hedged with 70% fixed-rate debt at 4.2% and dynamic curtailment optimization software boosting portfolio yields by 8%.

AeroGreen is positioned at the intersection of policy, tech, and demand. We're delivering contracted cash flows in a world where renewables' share hits 45% of global power by 2030.

Now, I'll hand the call over to Sarah Chen to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, John. Our financial performance in Q3 was exceptional. Revenue reached $285 million, representing a 28% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 32.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $85 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $50 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $450 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

I'll now turn to our perspective on the policy and regulatory landscape, which continues to be a tailwind for AeroGreen Energy and the broader clean tech sector. The macroeconomic environment remains supportive, but it's the evolving policy framework that's truly accelerating deployment and manufacturing scale-up. Starting domestically in the U.S., the Inflation Reduction Act remains the gold standard for clean energy incentives, and its impacts are materializing faster than anticipated. Through the first nine months of 2024, IRA-driven investments in solar PV and energy storage manufacturing have surpassed $25 billion—up 35% year-over-year. For us, this translates directly to our balance sheet: our 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Tax Credit claims are on track to generate $450 million in credits for FY2024, based on our 12 GW nameplate capacity across four U.S. module fabs in Ohio, Texas, and Arizona. We've hit 95% domestic content on our TOPCon bifacial modules, qualifying for the full 30% ITC adder, which boosted our effective project IRR by 200-300 basis points on our 2.5 GW utility-scale pipeline.

Permitting reforms are another bright spot. The FAST-41 designations we've secured for three hyperscaler-backed projects in the ERCOT and PJM queues have shaved interconnection timelines from 3-4 years to under 18 months. However, we're vigilant on risks: the 1.2 million MW U.S. interconnection backlog could delay 150 GW of additions through 2026 if FERC Order 2020 implementation lags. Our strategy is proactive: we've pre-filed 800 MW of co-located solar-plus-storage projects under the new queue reforms, positioning us ahead of competitors.

Regionally, California and Texas exemplify bifurcated dynamics. In CA, the Self-Generation Incentive Program has allocated $1.2 billion in 2024 for behind-the-meter storage, driving 25% YoY growth in our residential microinverter deployments—now at 150,000 units quarterly. Texas benefits from ERCOT's capacity auction premiums, where our 500 MW/1 GWh BESS portfolio fetched $15 million in ancillary service revenues last quarter alone.

Shifting to Europe, the REPowerEU plan and EU Green Deal are fueling a 42 GW solar addition target for 2024-2025. The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism is reshaping supply chains: we've localized 60% of our European polysilicon sourcing to Norway and Germany, mitigating 10-15% cost inflation from import tariffs. Our 1.2 GW ground-mount portfolio in Spain and Italy qualifies for €270 billion Recovery and Resilience Facility grants, with EPC margins expanding to 18% on average. A key trend is the rush for hybrid assets—our 300 MW wind-solar-storage hybrids in Poland are leveraging the revised TEN-E Regulation for cross-border grid priority.

In Asia-Pacific, China's dual carbon goals dominate, but U.S. and EU tariffs—now at 50%+ on Southeast Asian modules—are creating opportunities for our Vietnam fab expansion. We've ramped to 5 GW annual capacity there, exporting 70% to tariff-exempt markets like India and Australia. India's PLI scheme has awarded us a 2 GW thin-film allocation, yielding INR 15 billion in subsidies. ASEAN's grid modernization sees our 100 MWh liquid-cooled BESS pilots in Thailand testing virtual power plant aggregation under new protocols.

Globally, COP28's tripling of renewables pledge is on track, with IRENA forecasting 6,700 GW additions by 2030—but execution hinges on supply chain resilience. We've seen module prices stabilize at $0.28/W for mono PERC, down 12% QoQ, thanks to U.S. 45X incentives spurring 30 GW of new capacity. N-type TOPCon and HJT cells are policy-favored via technology-neutral PTC/ITC extensions through 2032, lowering LCOE to $25-30/MWh unsubsidized.

Strategically, we're derisking via policy advocacy—our $5 million PAC spend targets bipartisan permitting bills; hedged geography—45% U.S., 30% Europe, 25% APAC revenue mix insulates against election volatility; and innovation lock-in—partnering with NREL on perovskite tandems for 35%+ efficiency, qualifying for ARPA-E grants worth $50 million.

The regulatory environment is our biggest accelerant, supporting 25-30% CAGR in our backlog to $18 billion. We're well-positioned to capture share amid tightening domestic content rules and grid urgency.

Diving deeper into one key driver of our backlog stability: PPA pricing trends and contract extensions. Our portfolio relies heavily on these for predictable cash flows, and despite headwinds, we're seeing resilient dynamics. Utility-scale solar PPAs averaged $21/MWh on an LCOE-equivalent basis in Q3, up from $19/MWh in Q2 and contrasting sub-$18/MWh troughs in 2022. This lift comes from BOS cost inflation up 8-10% YoY, EPC margin compression for realistic IRRs, and premiums for dispatchable resources amid curtailment spikes.

Wind pricing averaged $28/MWh onshore, $60-70/MWh offshore. Hybrid solar-plus-storage PPAs, 35% of our signings, commanded $32-38/MWh. Our 450 MWdc Gemini Solar + Storage just locked a 15-year extension with NV Energy at $35/MWh fixed.

In the U.S. Southwest, pricing is $18-22/MWh, but corporate PPAs from hyperscalers pay 15% premiums. ERCOT signed 1.2 GW at $26/MWh, with batteries at $45/kW-year. Europe extended at €35-40/MWh, buoyed by subsidies. APAC pivots to India's $30/MWh auctions.

In Q3, we executed 800 MW extensions, adding $1.2 billion to backlog at 12% uplift. Our 250 MW Desert Sun wind extended to 2034 at $28/MWh with CPI escalator, accretes $150 million EBITDA. High-resolution SCADA, drone O&M at 98.5% availability, bifacial retrofits lifting yield 15-20%, and storage integrations justify premiums.

We're blending fixed PPAs with 20-30% merchant exposure, 2% COLA escalators, 'evergreen' clauses, and green hydrogen offtakes. Q4 solar PPAs firm at $23-25/MWh, extensions accelerate to 1.2 GW in 2025.

On gross and operating margins, which reflect structural improvements across our platforms. Gross margins hit 32.5% for Q3, up 450 bps YoY from 28.0% and 230 bps sequentially. Trailing 12-month average 31.1%, ahead of peers.

Utility-scale solar (62% revenue): 35.8%, module costs down 22% to $0.22/W, TOPCon at 23.5% efficiency. BESS (28%): 28.4%, LFP at $60/kWh, 92% efficiency. Offshore wind (10%): 22.1%, offset by 55-60% capacity factors.

Americas (75% revenue): 34.2% on IRA ITCs, $35/MWh PPAs. EMEA (15%): 27.8%, offset by grants. APAC (10%): 30.1% on PLI.

Supply chain diversification 65% away from single-country, manufacturing automation reducing COGS 12%, larger projects spreading costs.

Operating margins expanded to 15.2% from 12.1% YoY, adjusted 17.4%. SG&A leverage to 10.2%, R&D to 4.8%, lower interest. Guide FY2025 gross 34-36%, op 17-19%.

On debt levels and financing costs, total gross debt at $5.2 billion, up 8% YoY from construction financing. Net debt $3.1 billion, 3.4x net debt-to-EBITDA, within 3.0-4.0x target. 85% long-term, 12.4-year maturity, 72% fixed.

Interest expense guidance $210-230 million, 4.1% cost, down 70 bps. $1.2 billion green bond at 3.5%, refinancing legacy loans. IRA transferability reduced WACC to 5.8%.

U.S. sub-4% via DOE guarantees, Europe Euribor +225 bps mitigated by Taxonomy bonds, APAC stable. Deleveraging via $600 million sale-leasebacks, targeting $2.8 billion net debt. A- rating unlocks green bond market.

Our debt profile supports margin expansion and 12-15% ROIC.

Significant market trends: Renewables 95% of 2023 additions, solar 447 GWac. BNEF projects 7.3 TW by 2030. Solar LCOE $24-36/MWh, storage $120/kWh. Boosted our IRR to 12-14%, 420 bps EBITDA expansion.

IRA unlocked $110 billion investment, Europe 46 GW corporate PPAs. APAC manufacturing reshoring. Challenges: queues, disruptions—we're ahead with 75% LGIA.

Storage boom 100 GWh 2023, AI data centers 35 GW demand. $1.2 billion CapEx for tandems, iron-air, hydrogen. Positions for 25-30% CAGR.

For full-year context, FY2023 revenue $2.82 billion, 52% growth; Q4 $812 million, 61% YoY. EBITDA $728 million, 68% up, 25.8% margin. Solar $1.45 billion 64% growth, wind $685 million 42%, ESS $512 million 89%, services $165 million 31%.

North America 58% $1.64 billion 67%, Europe 24%, APAC 13%. Operational excellence 92% utilization, cost deflation, R&D breakthroughs. FY2024 guide 40-45% growth to $3.95-4.10 billion.

I'll now turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss our project development activities.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, with a record 4.2 GW added in Q3, bringing our global late-stage pipeline to 28.6 GW across solar, wind, storage, and hybrids—a 28% YoY increase. We focus on high-quality sites with superior irradiance, wind speeds, and BESS co-location.

Utility-scale solar: 2.1 GW added, including 1.2 GWdc Gemini Expansion in Nevada, 900 MWdc Arizona with Meta PPAs at $45/MWh. Onshore wind + hybrid: 1.5 GW, 850 MWac Traverse Wind hybrid in MISO. Storage/H2: 600 MW/400 MWh, HydroForge 200 MW electrolyzer with Air Products.

U.S. 72% (20.7 GW), Europe 15%, APAC/LATAM rest.

Q3 milestones: 1.8 GW CODs—Desert Bloom 450 MWac, Blacksnake 300 MW, Falcon 150 MW/600 MWh BESS. FID/NTP on 1.2 GW + 400 MW. 1.5 GW new PPAs, including AWS vPPA.

Hub-and-spoke strategy, next-gen integrations. Expect 3-4 GW Q4 adds, 2.5 GW CODs for FY25 $4.2 billion revenue.

Dr. Lisa Wong, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on groundbreaking technologies that enhance efficiency, reliability, and affordability. We've made significant breakthroughs in advanced solar panel technologies like perovskite tandems targeting 35% efficiency, energy storage solutions including iron-air for long-duration, and smart grid technologies with AI-driven optimization. These will revolutionize the energy landscape, lowering LCOE and enabling grid stability.

Next, Tom Greer will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Tom Greer:
Thank you, Lisa. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture. We're committed to minimizing environmental impact, with ambitious goals for reducing carbon emissions, improving energy efficiency, and responsible resource management. We're actively engaged in community initiatives and local sustainability programs, achieving 98% fleet availability while advancing biodiversity in project sites.

Now, Karen Lopez will provide operational highlights.

Karen Lopez:
Thank you, Tom. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We're optimizing operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring reliability of our assets. Best-in-class practices in asset management, maintenance, and supply chain, plus heavy investment in employee training, deliver 92% utilization and 15-20% cost synergies.

Raj Singh, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Karen. We're executing our long-term plan: expanding in key markets, diversifying offerings like green hydrogen and carbon capture, and strengthening partnerships. Our hub-and-spoke model and $300-400 million M&A targets position us for 15% CAGR.

Finally, Emily Novak, can you address our risk management strategies?

Emily Novak:
Thank you, Raj. We've implemented robust strategies to mitigate market, regulatory, and environmental risks. Continuous monitoring, proactive hedging—85% construction debt—and supply chain diversification keep us agile amid queues, rates, and policy shifts.

I'll turn it back to John for closing remarks.

John Harlan:
Thank you all. In conclusion, AeroGreen Energy had a truly exceptional Q3. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, commitment to innovation, and focus on sustainability will drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Tim Green with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tim Green:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Lisa Wong:
Thanks for the question, Tim. Green hydrogen is a key priority, with $150 million capex allocated for our 50 MW electrolyzer in Texas using PEM tech for under $2/kg production. We've got a pioneering 200 MW HydroForge project with DOE funding and Air Products offtake, scaling to contribute 5% EBITDA growth by H2 2025. This integrates with our 300 MW solar feed-in, positioning us in the $1.2 trillion hydrogen economy.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

John Harlan:
Great question, Maria. Competition is heating up, but our edge is in our 28.6 GW late-stage pipeline, 85% contracted with investment-grade off-takers, and vertical integration from modules to O&M. We've derisked 90% of U.S. queues, hedged geography across regions, and lead in hybrids with 35%+ efficiency tandems. Disciplined M&A like our Clearway buy and policy advocacy keep us ahead, targeting 12-15% ROIC.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

Emily Novak:
Thanks, David. Climate change brings extremes like heatwaves boosting ancillary revenues—our Falcon BESS captured $250/MWh peaks—but also risks like floods. We've stress-tested assets with dynamic modeling, invested in resilient designs like taller wind hubs, and diversified sites. Our risk framework includes insurance, 98.5% availability via drone O&M, and nature-based solutions, turning challenges into opportunities like higher curtailment optimization yields.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Sarah Chen:
Lisa, long-term profitability is strong, with backlog IRRs north of 12% levered, gross margins guiding 34-36%, and EBITDA 27-29%. PPAs with 2% escalators, extensions at 12-15% uplifts, and LCOE deflation to $25/MWh unsubsidized support this. Debt costs at 4.1%, IRA credits stacking to 50% ITC, and storage premiums in ERCOT/CAISO yield 20% ROIC through 2030, with 35 GW visibility.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to John Harlan for any closing remarks.

John Harlan:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of AeroGreen Energy. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
